text: DSH Coding Agents 是面向 Web 客户端的 DSH 编程助手插件，在设置页加入编程助手面板，并向 DSH agent 提供工具，可连接本机 Codex 与 Claude Code。用户可以搜索和分页查看两种工具的历史会话，新建、继续或分叉任务并查看运行状态，也可以重命名、标记、归档、回滚或删除会话，以及读取和编辑配置。适合在 DSH 中统一处理本地编程助手会话和任务的用户。需要本机已安装并登录相应 CLI；Codex 与 Claude Code 可分别使用。

DSH Coding Agents adds a settings panel and agent tools for local Codex and Claude Code. Search session history, run or resume tasks, manage sessions, and edit configuration from DSH. A local, logged-in CLI is required for each engine.
想从 DSH 里搜索 Codex 和 Claude Code 的历史会话
能不能在一个设置页面里查看和管理本地编程助手
我想让编程助手继续之前的会话，或者从旧会话分叉一个新任务
帮我按关键词或工作区找以前的编程对话
I want to start or resume a local Codex or Claude Code task from DSH.
How can I inspect and update my coding agent settings in one place?
DSH Coding Agents 的功能「搜索与阅读会话」：通过 agent 工具或设置页按引擎、关键词和工作区筛选 Codex 与 Claude Code 历史，并分页查看较长的消息记录。
DSH Coding Agents 的功能「运行编程任务」：用户可选择 Codex 或 Claude Code，新建、继续或分叉会话，提交提示词并查看运行输出和状态，也可取消正在运行的任务。
DSH Coding Agents 的功能「会话与配置管理」：从面板或工具重命名、标记、归档、回滚和删除会话，并读取或编辑引擎配置。

[](LICENSE)
[](#requirements)

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

The plugin calls the public, stable local interfaces of Codex and Claude Code. It never parses or rewrites their private databases, and every write goes through the vendor's own configuration protocol or a backup-plus-atomic-replace.

dsh-coding-agents README · Requirements：| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| DSH | 0.2.1-rc.5 (Cordis `4.0.5`, `@deepseek-ai/*` 0.2.1-rc.5) |
| Node.js | `^22.19.0 \|\| ^24.0.0` |
| Host services | `webServer`, `subprocess`, `tools` |
| Client services | `slots` (registers one section under Settings → Coding agents) |
| Vendor CLIs | Your own Codex CLI `>= 0.100.0` / Claude Code via Agent SDK `>= 0.3.0` (both optional peers) |

dsh-coding-agents README · Use your own Codex & Claude Code：The plugin never pins a vendor version. Each engine resolves independently, in order: `config.codexCommand` / `config.claudeCommand` → system `PATH` (`codex` / `claude`) → the CLI bundled in this package → unavailable with an actionable message. The status page reports the source (`config` / `system` / `bundled`) and the version read from `<cli> --version`.
section: Use your own Codex & Claude Code

text:
dsh-coding-agents README · Use your own Codex & Claude Code：- **Global install:** install Codex / Claude Code normally (e.g. `npm i -g @openai/codex`); the plugin drives the CLI already on your `PATH`, including future upgrades.
- **Install it in this profile:** `dsh plugin --profile <name> add @openai/codex` (or `pnpm add @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) — both are *optional peers*, so the plugin never dictates your version.
- **Point at a specific build** in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:
section: Use your own Codex & Claude Code

text:
dsh-coding-agents README · Use your own Codex & Claude Code：```yaml
- id: dsh-coding-agents
  config:
    codexCommand: /opt/homebrew/bin/codex
    claudeCommand: /Users/me/.local/bin/claude

Without the Claude Agent SDK the plugin still loads and the Codex engine keeps working; the Claude Code row simply reports `unavailable` with the SDK install hint.
section: Use your own Codex & Claude Code

text:
dsh-coding-agents README · Install：The package ships `cordis.patch.yml` and a `dsh.bundle.patch` declaration, so it installs as a bundle:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-coding-agents
```

Or add one loader entry to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: dsh-coding-agents
      name: 'dsh-coding-agents'
```

Restart the profile, then open **Settings → Coding agents**.

dsh-coding-agents README · What you can do：- Search the local session history of both Codex and Claude Code, and page through very long transcripts.
- Start, continue or fork a native session, watch text, tool calls and run state live, and cancel a run.
- Rename, tag, archive, unarchive, roll back and delete sessions. Operations that do not apply to an engine are refused explicitly instead of failing silently.
- Inspect configuration values, their effective values and their origin. Codex writes through its official config protocol; Claude Code uses backup plus atomic replace.
- The same capabilities are exposed to the DSH agent as six `coding_agent_*` tools, not only through the settings page.

dsh-coding-agents README · Natural-language examples：- "List the most recent Codex and Claude Code sessions."
- "Find the history that mentions the login failure."
- "Continue that Codex session and run the tests."
- "Start a Claude Code task in this workspace and fix the build error."
- "Read the current Codex configuration."

dsh-coding-agents README · Natural-language examples：The plugin only drives engines that the current user has installed and logged in. Runs default to workspace-write permissions, and full access is never reachable from a web page or from a model tool: it only happens when you start the run yourself in the DSH UI.

dsh-coding-agents README · Safety boundaries：- **Loopback + same-origin HTTP only.** `/coding-agents-api` rejects any request whose TCP peer is not this machine (403), any browser request whose `Origin` is not exactly the `http://<host>` it was sent to (403), any request whose `Sec-Fetch-Site` is `cross-site` (403), every POST without `content-type: application/json` (415), and CORS preflight (`OPTIONS`, 405). A random web page therefore cannot drive your local Codex or Claude Code, even with a "simple" request that skips the CORS preflight.
- **No full access through HTTP.** The HTTP surface accepts only `read-only` and `workspace-write`; `full-access` (Claude Code `bypassPermissions`, Codex `danger-full-access`) is reachable only from the DSH UI, where you confirm it yourself. The model tools mirror this ceiling: `coding_agent_run` refuses `full-access` with an actionable error.
- **Registered workspaces bound every `cwd`.** A `cwd` is accepted only when it resolves inside a workspace registered in DSH; paths are normalised and traversal outside a registered root is refused. When the host exposes no workspace registry, requests carrying a `cwd` are refused instead of trusting the

dsh-coding-agents README · Development：```bash
npm install
npm run typecheck   # source + client + tests
npm run build       # tsc → lib/, esbuild → lib/client.js
npm test            # vitest

`lib/client.js` is a `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })` closure factory, statically verified and executed in a sandbox by `scripts/verify-client.mjs`. The host contract is verified by `scripts/verify-host.mjs`: a real `@deepseek-ai/cordis` context loads the module, registers the route and tools, and cleans them up on dispose.

dsh-coding-agents README · Known limitations：- Requires a local Codex / Claude Code installation and login. Without it the engine reports an explicit unavailable state.
- Native executables are resolved on first use. If a package manager skipped the platform optional dependency, only that engine reports an actionable "unavailable" state (status page, `coding_agent_status`, run start) while the plugin itself still imports and the other engine keeps working; reinstall with optional dependencies enabled to restore it.
- The bundled CLI fallback (when present) is large, so the first install depends on network speed; using your own global CLI avoids it entirely.
- The HTTP API is a loopback `http://` surface by design: a TLS or non-loopback DSH web deployment is refused rather than downgraded.
- The plugin drives the vendor CLIs; it does not reimplement their agent loops.
